question.text: What is the textbook difference between a day order and a GTC (Good Till Cancelled) order, where GTC is available?

answer.text: A day order expires at the end of the trading day if unexecuted; a GTC order remains in the system until executed or explicitly cancelled
A day order can only be placed during the first hour; a GTC order can be placed anytime
A day order has a limit price; a GTC order is always a market order
A day order is for intraday positions; a GTC order is for delivery positions

explanation.text: The Logic: By textbook definition, a day order automatically expires at market close if not filled, while a GTC order persists across trading days until matched or cancelled. GTD (Good Till Date) orders expire on a specified date. The Trap: Both order types can be placed any time during trading hours, can carry limit prices, and are not tied to intraday vs delivery distinctions. Note: Per NISM Series IV (pp.207-208), GTC and GTD orders are currently NOT available on the system as per SEBI directives — the difference above describes the conceptual/textbook definition only.
